acceptance.output_evidence:
RECORDED FOR L9, NO VERDICT.

1. WHICH ATTRIBUTION CAN RECONCILE TO THE CENT AND STILL BE ECONOMICALLY WRONG. Three, named with the fixture and whether I built it.
(i) COT'S RECURSIVE MODEL ATTRIBUTION. `expand_model()` on `fact_model_blend` distributes each account's TOTAL custody value across the resolved leaves by weight. The ACCOUNT total (sum of all leaf TARGET values plus any unresolved mass) reconciles PERFECTLY to the cent by construction -- every dollar is either assigned a leaf or counted as unresolved mass, with nothing dropped or double-counted. But the WEIGHTS THEMSELVES are `fact_model_blend.relative_allocation`/`absolute_allocation`, read AS-IS from Rebalancer's own blend table. If Rebalancer's blend percentages are stale relative to the account's ACTUAL current sleeve composition (a rebalance that has not yet posted, a manual override BD recorded elsewhere), the TOTAL still reconciles to the cent while every individual leaf's dollar figure is wrong -- a total that is right for the wrong reason. FIXTURE: NOT BUILT. I tested that the ARITHMETIC of the split is correct (weights sum, cycles/missing retain mass, nothing renormalizes) but I built no fixture comparing a blend weight against an INDEPENDENT source of the account's actual current holdings composition, because no such independent source was in this cell's grant -- `fact_holdings` gives the account TOTAL, not a per-model breakdown to check the blend against.
(ii) 49F'S ALLOCATION-TO-MODEL LINK. The account node's value comes from `fact_allocation_valuation` (equity+cash); the model_id comes from a SEPARATE table, `fact_allocation_account_map`. Both are dated `date=%s` (same partition), so they are SYNCHRONIZED for this run, but if SmartX ever landed a map update ahead of a valuation update (or vice versa) on a single day, the reported model assignment could be for a MODEL THE ACCOUNT HAS SINCE LEFT, with the value still correct. FIXTURE: NOT BUILT -- I did not construct a same-account-different-model-across-two-partitions test.
(iii) INF'S managed_value ATTRIBUTION TO A SINGLE model_id. `portfolios_full.managed_value` is the PORTFOLIO's total; `portfolios_simple.model_id` names ONE model per portfolio. If a portfolio is genuinely a BLEND of models at the Eclipse layer (my read of `portfolios_simple`/`portfolios_full` found no blend/child columns the way COT's `fact_model_blend` has them, so I could not confirm Eclipse portfolios are single-model by construction rather than by this cell's incomplete read of the schema), the whole managed value would attribute to one model when it should split. FIXTURE: NOT BUILT, and this head is the one I am least certain about -- I did not find an Eclipse blend table within this cell's time budget and cannot rule out that one exists.

2. WHICH SOURCE CLOCKS WERE MIXED, AND HOW THE SNAPSHOT STATES IT. Two real mixes, both STATED in the contract, not hidden. (i) 49F: the account map/roster (`fact_allocation_account_map`, `fact_model_allocation_roster`) and the valuation (`fact_allocation_valuation`) are read from the SAME `date=` partition, resolved by `_latest_date_partition` against the MAP table specifically -- so if the valuation table's OWN latest complete partition were a different date than the map's, this cell would silently read a valuation partition dated one step behind what the map's date implies, and NOTHING checks the two dates agree beyond both being requested under the same `date=` string. `clocks.source_as_of` in the emitted contract carries only ONE source/date pair per firm today, which UNDERSTATES this: SmartX's roster/map/valuation are three tables that could each have their own true completion date, and this cell reports one date for all three rather than three independent `source_as_of` entries the way `source_set_revision` COULD carry them (the schema supports an array; this cell populates it with one element). (ii) COT: `assign_date`/`blend_date`/`roster_date`/`value_date` are FOUR INDEPENDENTLY resolved dates (assignment 2026-08-30, blend 2026-08-30, roster 2026-08-30, value 2026-09-09 in this run) and ALL FOUR are carried in `manifest`, so the mix is explicit in the artifact the battery reads -- but only ONE of the four (`source_completion_date`, tied to `value_date`) reaches the SHARED contract's `clocks.business_date` field; a consumer reading only the contract (not this runner's internal manifest) cannot see that the model assignment is 10 days older than the custody value it is laid over.

3. WHAT A READER CANNOT LEARN FROM THE SNAPSHOT ALONE. (i) That INF's model attribution might be incomplete for genuinely blended Eclipse portfolios (head 1(iii) above) -- nothing in the contract flags a portfolio as possibly-blended. (ii) That COT's model weights are read as-is from Rebalancer with no cross-check against actual current sleeve holdings (head 1(i)). (iii) That 49F's model link and its valuation could theoretically be off by one partition if the two tables' true completion dates ever diverge (head 2(i)) -- the contract's single `source_completion_date` cannot express three tables' three clocks. (iv) The `directory_cross_check` field (row IRPT_BCKEND-W1-S7) is NOT part of the shared contract at all -- it lives only in this runner's internal manifest, so a consumer reading the PUBLISHED `snapshot.json` cannot see that the directory-population cross-check failed for 2 of 3 firms; that fact is visible only to someone reading this cell's own manifest or this proof. (v) Whether `unresolved_mass` in a COT account's coverage remainder is GENUINELY unattributable or merely a gap in this cell's own blend-table read -- the contract states the amount and 'inferred' as its provenance claim, but not WHICH.
acceptance.denominator: 3 attribution risks named with 0 of 3 fixtures built and a stated reason each; 2 source-clock mixes named (49F 3-table single-date read, COT 4 independently-dated fields vs 1 contract field); 5 things a reader cannot learn from the snapshot alone

mutant.description: The load-bearing claims are that every dollar is attributed exactly once with weights applied exactly once, that a cycle or missing node never silently loses mass or lets a renormalization hide it, and that a pie never mixes bases. FOUR red-first mutants directly on the mechanism, plus the REAL BUG a fixture caught in production code (not a mutant -- a genuine first-draft defect).
mutant.expected: Each mutant must fail at least one test (rc=1), and restore byte-for-byte.
mutant.observed:
4 of 4 FIRED-AS-EXPECTED. Reintroducing decompose()'s invalid []-on-cycle shape failed 2 tests (test_3_cycle_retains_weight_as_unresolved_mass_not_dropped, test_3_partial_cycle_retains_only_the_cyclic_share). Disabling the never-renormalize guarantee failed 2 (test_4_missing_child_node_retains_weight_as_unresolved_mass, test_5_surviving_sibling_keeps_its_original_fraction_never_rescaled). Double-applying an edge weight failed the SAME 2 (a different mechanism, same symptom class -- both distort the weight distribution). Disabling assert_bases_not_spliced entirely failed 1 (test_bases_never_spliced_refuses_a_mixed_pie). All four restored byte-for-byte (sha256 compared, 4 of 4 equal), 22 of 22 tests green before and after the whole exercise.
SEPARATELY: the FIRST DRAFT of build_inf put an OBSERVED 'excluded' node and an ASSIGNED 'model' node as siblings under one account -- assert_bases_not_spliced correctly RAISED on this cell's OWN real 2026-09-11 data (not a fixture, not a mutant), which is the strongest evidence the mechanism is not merely testing itself: it caught a genuine defect in the code it ships beside. Fixed by restructuring the node hierarchy (managed/excluded as two OBSERVED siblings, the ASSIGNED model view descending from managed alone), never by loosening the check.
